name: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd
title: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd - 540133 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Life insurer grew VNB 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9% on negative persistency and assumption changes; growth guidance withheld.

summary.headline: ICICI Pru Life FY26 VNB rose 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9%.
summary.overview: FY26 showed absolute VNB growth of 10.9% to ₹26.29bn and VNB margin expansion to 24.7% (from 22.8%), while APE grew just 2.2% to ₹106.41bn. Retail protection was the standout, up 32.3% for the year and 60.5% in Q4, offsetting weak agency, direct, linked and annuity lines. Profit after tax rose 34.6% to ₹16bn, helped by a ₹1.14bn gain on sale of ICICI Pension Fund Management Company; excluding it, PAT grew 25%. EV operating assumption changes (GST input-tax-credit loss, persistency) and a ₹2.64bn persistency variance (mainly the 100% premium back annuity) pulled RoEV down to 11.9%. Management said West Asia disruption hurt March new business across all lines except protection, and it deferred Ind-AS adoption by a year via forbearance.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 32.3% YoY in FY26 and 60.5% in Q4; 13% of addressable population covered. Protection mix rose 2.2pp to 17.9% of VNB mix.

segments.name: Group protection
segments.commentary: Up 7.1% YoY; group term +14.6%, credit life +1.8%. Group business overall +14.5%, 18.3% of APE.

segments.name: Linked (ULIP)
segments.commentary: APE up 1.6% YoY; two-year CAGR 14.2%. Focus on high sum assured ULIP to cushion market volatility.

segments.name: Non-linked savings
segments.commentary: APE grew 15.4% YoY for nine months but declined YoY in Q4 as a prior-year Q4 launch normalised; full year roughly flat. Par:non-par roughly 2:1.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Four-year CAGR about 20%; stabilised at about 7% of retail mix. Heavy single-pay skew and 100% premium back product drove persistency issues.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹26.86bn; with direct, 47.4% of retail APE. Growth weak on high annuity base, but improving sequentially through the year.

segments.name: Direct channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹14.30bn; growth lagged on base effects. Focus on NRI via GIFT City and online channel.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 3.6% YoY; 29.8% of APE. 53 bank partnerships with access to 26,400+ branches.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 23.4% YoY; 13.2% of APE. Over 1,500 non-bank partnerships.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 growth number given; management called the environment volatile and said it is too early to commit.
Long-term RoEV expected at 13-14%, depending on yield curve and VNB growth; RoEV to become less significant once Ind-AS is adopted.
Management said VNB margin of 24.7% (with persistency and mortality/expense assumptions now set) is the baseline going forward.
Ind-AS go-live deferred by a year via forbearance; current-year results remain on existing I-GAAP with Ind-AS as alternate financials.
Would reprice non-par products if the yield curve moves down; no en masse repricing so far, only cohort-level changes (1-3% at some peers).
capex_capacity: Distribution: 2.42 lakh+ advisers, 53 bank partnerships, 1,500+ non-bank partnerships.
Agency strategy centres on micro-market-led branch expansion and technology/analytics productivity tools.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict hurt new business in March 2026 across all products except protection, per management.
Industry retail sum assured grew 2.5x in the post-GST-reform period versus pre-reform; GST removed 18% on retail protection.
Non-par sales are constrained because bank FD rates are steep relative to G-Sec-linked pricing, so customers switch products.
Management said it has not cut prices en masse; the yield curve benefit was retained rather than passed to customers.

Persistency: 61st month decline attributed to a regulatory definition change; 25th month decline seen as spillover from 13th month, largely annuity-driven. Non-linked 13th-month persistency fell from 86.8% to 73.2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth strategy and non-par outlook, and what is the par/non-par mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth outlook not committed given volatility. Par:non-par mix roughly 2:1 for the year, with some quarters higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency experience built into VNB margin assumptions, and what about surrender value regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency is reviewed at year-end; permanent changes go into assumptions and temporary ones run through variances. Early surrender-value product experience is not yet showing a material difference after 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is agency growing slowly, and how will it be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency was held back by a high annuity base in the prior year. The 3-year CAGR is about 12-13%; micro-market-led agency strategy is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Did the West Asia war affect new business, and how does demand differ across products?
qa_highlights.answer: March new business was hit across the board except protection. Management declined to quantify the impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ind-AS transition plan and its capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forbearance sought for one year, citing awaited joint expert group clarity on CSM inputs. Solvency stays on the existing basis (227%) until RBC is implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 2.5pp economic variance uplift in VNB margin, and was pricing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield curve gains were held in economic assumptions, while product repricing sits in new business profile. Pricing was not materially changed; cost efficiencies were used to hold prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EV split between VIF and net worth reclassified?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder share of MTM on policyholder-fund assets and derivatives moved from net worth to VIF to align with market practice. Total EV is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.64bn persistency variance related to FY26 VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost none of it relates to FY26 business; it is entirely back-book.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not aware of discussions beyond data requests from the regulator; distributor remuneration talks are continuous.

risks_watch: APE growth of 2.2% against market growth of 10-11% (two-year CAGR ~7-8% vs market 10-11%); share loss risk.
Persistency weakness in annuity, 13th/25th/61st month cohorts; surrender-value regulation effects are still unknown.
GST input-tax-credit loss and pricing lag; operating assumption change of -0.5% of opening EV.
Geopolitical volatility weighing on March and April sales; FY27 growth guidance withheld.
Possible regulatory commission cuts; management gave no sensitivity.
Ind-AS transition and RBC solvency regime changes; the next-year forbearance outcome is open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on VNB, margins and protection momentum, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 growth. Management was evasive on non-par pricing, commission regulation and the drivers of the persistency decline. It acknowledged the agency and direct channel shortfall and the below-market APE growth.
key_quotes: As we celebrate 25 years of service to our customers, we would like to reaffirm our commitment to deliver sustainable VNB growth by balancing business growth, profitability and risk and prudence.

Our focus is on growing the absolute VNB, which we have been able to achieve through improvement in product mix and operational efficiencies even after accounting for the unavailability of input tax credit.
So, if we were to actually start to cut margins to be able to deliver on growth on non-par, it may not be accretive to shareholders.
I think one of the biggest tailwinds that we have got as an industry has been the GST reform, and that is felt most in protection.

financial_highlights.change: Around 13% before assumption changes and variances

growth.why: No FY27 growth number was given and management said it was too early to commit, with no capacity or capex disclosed; FY26 APE grew only 2.2% and March new business was hit by West Asia disruption, so the outlook is unclear.
